field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No browser, admin site or Django request was run; the finding is static. The upstream regression test was read, not executed.

Reachability requires limit_choices_to (or a callable returning it) to contain a value an attacker can influence. Django models normally declare it statically; the flaw matters when an application derives those values from request data or stores attacker-controlled strings in them.

The NVD Spanish description is a mistranslation that describes CVE-2020-13254 (memcached key collision), not this CVE. The English description, the Django announcement, OSV and the fix commit all agree on ForeignKeyRawIdWidget. Only the English NVD text was used.
The MITRE CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS). CWE-79 and CVSS 3.1 6.1 come from NVD; GHSA/OSV agree on CWE-79 and call the severity MODERATE.

The 2.2.x fix commit 6d61860b has the subject prefix '[2.0.x]' even though the Django announcement maps it to the 2.2 release branch and git confirms it is an ancestor of tag 2.2.13. The subject text is recorded as-is; branch membership is established by tag ancestry, not by the prefix.

The master and 3.1.x changesets (2dd4d110, 49d7cc19) were identified from the announcement and git metadata but were not used as the vulnerable-commit basis; 3.1 was still alpha at release time and no 3.1 fixed release exists.
The canonical vulnerable commit is the 3.0.2 tag; the 2.2 branch has the same vulnerable code at 2.2.12 but the dataset snapshot for this repository is 3.0.2.
The snapshot inventory has 6163 tracked files and 67 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.
No downstream distribution backport (Ubuntu USN-4381-1/2, Debian DSA-4705, Fedora, NetApp, Oracle) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.

critical_operation.code_excerpt:
params = self.url_parameters()
            if params:
                related_url += '?' + '&'.join('%s=%s' % (k, v) for k, v in params.items())
            context['related_url'] = mark_safe(related_url)
critical_operation.description: ForeignKeyRawIdWidget.get_context interpolates every query parameter with a bare '%s=%s' format, joins them with '&', and then marks the whole URL safe. The values come from url_params_from_lookup_dict, which applies str() without percent-encoding, and from the related field name. Because mark_safe makes the result a SafeString, the admin template's href="{{ related_url }}" inserts the string without HTML escaping, so a value containing a quote can close the attribute and inject markup. The 3.0.7 and 2.2.13 fixes replace the join with django.utils.http.urlencode and stop calling mark_safe.

entry_point.description: Rendering an admin form that uses ForeignKeyRawIdWidget calls get_context. The widget collects query parameters from the related model's limit_choices_to and builds the lookup link, so a value in limit_choices_to reaches the unencoded join.

trace.description: base_url_parameters reads limit_choices_to and invokes it when callable
url_params_from_lookup_dict converts each value with str() and performs no URL encoding
get_context concatenates the parameters with '%s=%s' and '&' without escaping
mark_safe marks the concatenated URL as safe, disabling template autoescaping
the widget template writes related_url into href, so a quote in the value breaks out of the attribute
